shared-needs.rule: shared/ belongs to the shared author (brief C, "What R-03 produces"); this volume never writes it and never points into it before it exists. Each need names the volume and the anchor the shared author declares. check.sh (N-46) resolves a need by volume and anchor once the shared volume lands, so a need becomes a live pointer without a hand edit. The same needs are returned to the shared author as data by the seat that wrote this volume.
shared-needs.need: Rows for backup.started 100; backup 201; backup.busy 423; backup.failed 500; backup.mirror_failed 500; backup.rotten 500; backup.disk 503. Owner-acts: backup.failed; backup.rotten; backup.disk after N-45 ran; backup.mirror_failed when it persists a day.

backups(id, at, class, path, bytes, checksum, inner_checksum, top_seq, verified, mirror_path, mirror_checksum, pruned_at); entities backup:latest (compare-and-swap) and backup:running (expected absent).
Backups, logs and state live under the state root with a README and a cleanup script each (C35); the hand backup tree is disposed of by N-49.
No node selects the owner's privileged AWS profile; a cloud mirror is the owner's own user-initiated script (global hard rule).

backup.interval_seconds 21600, backup.min_interval_seconds 60, backup.snapshot_seconds 300, backup.verify_seconds 600, backup.mirror_seconds 600, backup.min_free_mib 2048, backup.retention {tick 48h, daily 30d, monthly 12mo, manual until card}, backup.mirror_dir optional.
The service restarts mid-run: temps under tmp/ removed at start, backup:running cleared, a due backup runs at once; nothing is lost because the live store is never the thing being written.
Free space under backup.min_free_mib: backup.disk 503 once, run skipped, N-45 cleanup, then one card if still under.

purpose.is: N-05 is the answer to the catch the owner asked about on C34 ("whats the catch here?"): one store on one host is one box, so the store is copied on a schedule, verified, classed for retention, mirrored off the box when a mirror is configured, and every copy is a record.
It is the only path by which N-01's restore runbook gets a file to restore from, and it is what cleanup-store.sh checks before it may delete the live file.
purpose.is-not: It does not prune (N-45 does, from the retention class on each backup record), does not back up the repository (git is its own backup), and never uses the owner's privileged AWS profile or any credential the owner did not place in the unit's environment.
purpose.decisions: D10 (C34: one store, backups scheduled per the catch), D04 (C35: artifacts in the state root with cleanup scripts), D22 (the host's crash history: eleven bugchecks in seven weeks, L10 section 5.3).

record.field: tick (every backup.interval_seconds 21600), daily (the first tick after 03:00Z), monthly (the first daily of a UTC month). The class is decided by N-06's schedule, not here, so the retention class is data on the tick.

also.from: N-50 before cut-over records, N-49 before each unlanded cleanup step (04-UNLANDED section 12 step 1), the restore runbook, and the ctl CLI
also.note: an extra backup of class manual; bounded by backup.min_interval_seconds 60
the source; the backup never opens coq.db as a second writer

record.field: sha256 of the compressed file; a second sha256 of the uncompressed database file inside.
The store's top seq at the moment of the snapshot, so a restore knows exactly which records it loses.
tick, daily, monthly, manual; N-45 keeps tick 48 h, daily 30 d, monthly 12 months, manual until the owner's cleanup card (backup.retention in config).
true: the copy was opened read-only, PRAGMA integrity_check returned ok, and its records count equals top_seq.
The mirror path and its checksum when backup.mirror_dir is configured, else absent; a failed mirror is backup.mirror_failed 500 and the local backup still counts.

output.record: After 3 attempts: the stage that failed (snapshot, compress, verify, write), the error, the attempts; one card through N-28 because a store with no fresh backup is an owner-acts state.

mechanism.component: Go package scheduler/internal/backup: Run(class), Verify(path), Prune is not here. It calls N-01's Snapshot, which runs VACUUM INTO on a temp path inside the store directory (same filesystem, so the rename is atomic), under the writer's turn so the copy is one transaction-consistent image.
zstd level 3 (the Go zstd library pinned in the module; no shelling out), streaming, so a 1 GiB file needs no 1 GiB of memory.

STATE/backup/store/YYYY/MM/ by the UTC day of the snapshot; one file per backup; a README.md at STATE/backup/store/ names the writer, the classes, the retention and the cleanup script (owner, C35: cleanup scripts for every artifact).

backup.mirror_dir, optional: a second directory on another filesystem (a Windows drive under /mnt, a network share, a USB disk). Copy then checksum compare; never the primary. No cloud target is built in: the owner's S3 bucket needs the privileged profile and that is user-initiated only (global hard rule), so a cloud mirror is a later owner-run script, not this node.
mechanism.mermaid: flowchart LR T[backup tick, class] --> S[N-01 Snapshot: VACUUM INTO tmp] S --> Z[zstd stream to tmp.zst] Z --> V[open tmp.zst read-only, integrity_check, count = top_seq] V -- ok --> R[rename to final path, fsync dir] V -- not ok --> F[attempt + 1, up to 3] R --> C[sha256 both, write README if absent] C --> M{mirror_dir set?} M -- yes --> Y[copy, checksum compare] M -- no --> B Y --> B[append backup 201] F --> B2[backup.failed 500 after 3]
mechanism.step: Ask N-01 for Snapshot(tmp): the writer goroutine runs VACUUM INTO tmp between two transactions; the snapshot's top_seq is returned with it.
Compress to tmp.zst; compute sha256 of the raw file while reading it.

Verify: decompress to a second temp file, open read-only, PRAGMA integrity_check must be exactly ok, SELECT count(*) FROM records must equal top_seq, SELECT max(seq) must equal top_seq. Any difference is a failed attempt.
Rename tmp.zst to the final path; fsync the directory; sha256 the compressed file.

Mirror when configured: copy to mirror_dir with the same relative path, read it back, compare sha256; a mismatch deletes the mirror copy and reports backup.mirror_failed 500 (3 attempts); the primary record is still 201.
Write the backups table row and append backup 201 with everything above; the entity backup:latest is CAS-updated so cleanup-store.sh and N-01's restore have one place to look.
Delete every temp file in STATE/backup/store/tmp/ older than one hour at the start of every run (a crashed run leaves temps; this is their cleanup).
mechanism.restore-drill: On the daily class, after the backup, run Verify on the newest backup of the previous day as well, so a backup that rotted on disk is found within a day and reported as backup.rotten 500.

start.rule: Nothing starts by an agent typing. N-06 emits the backup tick from the service clock; the schedule is config; the first tick after start runs at once when the newest backup is older than backup.interval_seconds (a restart never skips a due backup).
start.step: At start: create STATE/backup/store/ and tmp/ 0700; write README.md if absent; read the backups table for the newest verified row; if none or older than the interval, run a tick-class backup now.
Check free space under STATE against backup.min_free_mib 2048; under it, backup.disk 503 once and the run is skipped until N-45 frees space.
backup.started 100 with the newest backup's age.

wait.name: snapshot
wait.fallback: a failed attempt; the writer is released by context cancel; the store keeps serving

wait.name: compress-verify
wait.fallback: a failed attempt; temps are removed

wait.name: mirror
wait.fallback: backup.mirror_failed 500; the local backup stands; an unmounted mirror is reported once per transition, not per tick

wait.name: disk
wait.fallback: backup.disk 503; N-45 runs cleanup; owner card if still under after cleanup

wait.name: interval
wait.fallback: N-06 reports tick.missed when a tick is late by two intervals; the next tick runs

retries.rule: Every automated step retries up to 3 times, then recovers and reports.
retries.step: Any stage failing restarts the run from the snapshot, 3 attempts with 30, 60, 120 s between; the fourth is backup.failed 500 with the stage and the error; one card through N-28; the next scheduled tick tries again regardless, because a transient disk error should not need the owner to re-arm anything.
3 attempts inside the run; then backup.mirror_failed 500; the primary is not retried for a mirror failure.
A previous day's backup failing Verify is reported once; the next backup is not affected; the owner's card says which file and that newer ones verified.

many-agents.reading: Any node and the owner read the backups table and backup:latest; a seat never needs a backup; the restore runbook (N-01) reads the latest verified row.
many-agents.working: One backup runs at a time: the run takes the entity flag backup:running by CAS (expected absent) and releases it at the end; a backup.now while one runs returns backup.busy 423 and is not queued, because the next tick will cover it.
many-agents.collision: A scheduled tick and a backup.now in the same minute: the flag admits one; the other is 423; the one that ran is of the class that won; a manual class is never downgraded, so if the manual one lost, N-50 or N-49 retries after backup.min_interval_seconds and gets its manual copy.

The snapshot is one consistent image while Puts continue: VACUUM INTO in WAL mode reads a snapshot; writers are not blocked beyond the writer's single turn to start it; top_seq names the boundary exactly.
N-45 prunes while a backup writes: the new file is under tmp/ until rename, and N-45 prunes only rows in the backups table with a past retention date, so an in-progress backup is invisible to it.

The service restarts mid-run: the temp files are removed at the next start (step 7 of the mechanism), the flag backup:running is cleared by the start sequence, and the due check runs a backup at once.
many-agents.test: With the fake clock: 10 days of ticks with Puts between them, one backup.now storm of 5 calls, one injected verify failure and one injected disk-full: every record's class is right, exactly one run at a time, the failure retried 3 times and reported once, the disk-full skipped with one 503, and every surviving file verifies.

emits.acts: the caller of backup.now, which may retry after min_interval
N-41 alert; owner card only when it persists a day
owner, one card: a stored backup fails verification
N-45 cleanup, then owner through a card

status-codes.rule: Every code above must exist in ../../shared/status-codes.xml#codes with the same meaning and actor.

path.cleanup: scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-backups.sh: --dry-run lists files whose backups row is past its retention class and files with no row (orphans); --apply deletes them and marks the rows pruned; it never deletes the newest verified backup of any class, whatever its age
removed by the run itself at start; cleanup-backups.sh --apply removes anything left over an hour old
cleanup-backups.sh --mirror applies the same retention to the mirror; it refuses when the mirror is not mounted
rows are pruned with their files by cleanup-backups.sh

state-paths.rule: The hand backups under STATE/backup/2026/10/ (L02 S19) are a different tree: N-49 disposes of them; this node never writes there.

re-entry.note: backup.now of class manual before each cleanup or cut-over step

A verify failure is retried 3 times then reported once as backup.failed with the stage.

A restart mid-run leaves no temp file and runs a due backup at once.
item.proof: Test with a prepared tmp/ and a stale backups row.

item.check: The daily class also re-verifies yesterday's newest backup and reports backup.rotten on failure.

item.check: Mirror copies compare equal; a mismatch deletes the mirror copy and reports once.

No credential and no cloud call exist in the package.

actor.name: owner

gauge.name: backup.mirror_ok
gauge.note: 1 when the last mirror matched, 0 otherwise

monitoring.surface: Map screen (N-38) shows the backup machine with a lamp (fresh, due, failed); Stats (N-40) shows age and bytes; Alerts (N-41) shows backup.failed and backup.rotten; the Controls screen (N-42) has the backup-now button, which is an owner control.action through N-29.

runbook.task: `scheduler ctl backup list` prints every row with class, verified, top_seq, bytes, path, pruned.
`scheduler ctl backup now` (class manual); 423 means one is running; wait a minute.
`scheduler ctl backup verify PATH` runs the same Verify as the run.
See ../N-01/spec.xml#runbook restore; it takes the path from `backup list`.
Set backup.mirror_dir in scheduler/config/scheduler.json through a ticket to a mounted directory on another device; `scheduler ctl reload`; the next run mirrors.
